fact_checks.fact: In loco parentis refers to an individual with day-to-day responsibility for a child's care or financial support
fact_checks.evidence: In loco parentis affects FMLA leave provisions by considering a child for whom an employee has in loco parentis status as a child (son or daughter) of the employee. Additionally, a person who had in loco parentis status with respect to an employee when that employee was a child is considered the employee’s “parent.” A biological or legal relationship is not necessary.
